# Timezone-sensitive code has no timezone-discriminating coverage

## Context

Found while reviewing `#19004` (a first-time contributor's spec for `Neo.util.Date`). The spec is correct and thorough, and one of its arms still cannot fail on CI.

`Neo.util.Date.convertToyyyymmdd()` exists to return the **local** calendar day. Its whole mechanism is one correction:

```js
return new Date(date.getTime() - (date.getTimezoneOffset() * 60000)).toISOString().split('T')[0]
```

Remove that correction and the method returns the **UTC** calendar day instead. Measured on `dev@afddc57634`, `#19004`'s spec run twice with the correction deleted:

| runner timezone | result |
|---|---|
| `TZ=Europe/Berlin` (UTC+2) | **1 failed** — the arm catches it |
| `TZ=UTC` | **7 passed** — the regression is invisible |

Neither `.github/workflows/test.yml` nor `test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs` sets `TZ`, so every tier runs at the runner default — **UTC on GitHub-hosted runners**.

## The Problem

**Under UTC, the corrected and uncorrected implementations are identical.** That makes this a different class from a missing test case: no additional input closes it, because there is no input for which the two behaviours differ when the offset is zero. A contributor's green run on a European laptop is strictly stronger evidence than the same suite on CI, and nothing says so.

The consequence is not hypothetical: `#19004`'s `convertToyyyymmdd` arm looks like it pins the timezone correction, and in CI it pins nothing.

## The Architectural Reality

The class is **small and enumerable**, which is why this is worth closing rather than noting. Exactly two files under `src/` convert between local and UTC — `grep -rln "getTimezoneOffset\|toISOString" src/`:

| file | line | what it does | discriminating coverage today |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/util/Date.mjs` | `:52` | `convertToyyyymmdd` shifts by the local offset so `toISOString()` prints the **local** day | `#19004`'s arm — **only off-UTC** |
| `src/form/field/Date.mjs` | `:201` | `submitDateObject` builds `new Date(\`${value}T12:00:00.000Z\`)` — noon UTC, deliberately chosen so the calendar day survives every zone from UTC−11 to UTC+12 | none found |
| `src/form/field/Date.mjs` | `:203` | `isoDate` returns `new Date(value).toISOString()` — safe **only** while `value` is a date-only string, which ECMAScript parses as UTC; a local-format string would be parsed as local time | none found |

The `:201` noon-UTC trick is a correct and deliberate piece of engineering that **nothing currently protects**. It is exactly the kind of line a well-meaning simplification deletes.

## The Fix

Not prescribed — the shape is a real fork and the wrong choice makes the suite worse:

1. **Pin a non-UTC `TZ` for the whole unit tier.** One line. Also makes every *other* spec run off-UTC, which is a behaviour change for specs that are currently UTC-coincidental — and it would hide the opposite class of bug.
2. **A second Playwright project running the timezone-sensitive specs under a pinned non-UTC zone**, so both zones are covered and the default tier is untouched. Costs a config surface; `playwright.config.matrix.mjs` is the in-tree precedent for a separate runner with its own contract.
3. **Per-spec `TZ` control**, if Playwright's `timezoneId` reaches the unit tier's context — it does for browser contexts, and this tier's relationship to that needs checking before the option is real.

Whichever lands, the acceptance test is the same: **the mutation above must red.**

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Deleting the offset correction in `Neo.util.Date.convertToyyyymmdd` reds the suite **in CI**, not only on an off-UTC host. This is the falsifier; the fix is whatever makes it true.
- [ ] `src/form/field/Date.mjs`'s `submitDateObject` noon-UTC construction has an arm that reds when the `T12:00:00.000Z` literal is changed to `T00:00:00.000Z`.
- [ ] `src/form/field/Date.mjs`'s `isoDate` path has an arm covering a date-only input, with the parsing rule it relies on named in a comment.
- [ ] The chosen mechanism is documented where a spec author reads it, so the next date-adjacent spec knows which zone it runs in.
- [ ] Whichever option lands, the existing tiers stay green and the choice records why the other two were rejected.

## Out of Scope

- Changing any of the three implementations. All three are correct; this ticket is about whether a regression in them would be caught.
- A general audit of locale-dependent behaviour. The predicate here is narrow and greppable — `getTimezoneOffset` or `toISOString` in `src/` — and it returns two files.
- `#19004` itself, which is approved and correct. Its arm is as good as an arm can be under a UTC runner.

## Avoided Traps

- **Adding another date to `#19004`'s spec.** The instinct is to widen the input set; it cannot work. Under a zero offset the two implementations compute the same thing for every input.
- **Pinning `TZ=UTC`.** It would make the suite deterministic and permanently blind to exactly this class.
